questions.stemHtml: Each of the images in the diagram below illustrates a train of action potentials in response to a sudden limb movement. The sensory neuron encoding the velocity of the limb movement is illustrated by which of the following image?
questions.solutionHtml:
B

The IA afferents, which innervate the muscle spindles, have a phasic and tonic component. B illustrates the response of IA afferents to a sudden movement of a limb.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 129–132.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman, who has been immobilized with a sprained ankle for the past 4 days, develops a throbbing pain that has spread to her entire left leg. History reveals that she has been taking oral contraceptives for 15 years. Compared to localized pain, such as one might experience from a needle stick, which of the following is true of ischemic pain?

options.label: A
options.text: Ischemic pain sensory fibers are classified as A-delta (Ad) sensory fibers

options.label: B
options.text: Ischemic pain is produced by overstimulating somatic touch receptors

options.label: C
options.text: Ischemic pain is transmitted to the brain through the Neo spinothalamic tract

options.label: D
options.text: Ischemic pain sensory fibers terminate within the substantia gelatinosa of the spinal cord

questions.answerText: Ischemic pain sensory fibers terminate within the substantia gelatinosa of the spinal cord
questions.solutionHtml:
Ischemic pain sensory fibers terminate within the substantia gelatinosa of the spinal cord
  • This is a case of Deep Vein Thrombosis (given the risk factors of immobilization and history of Oral contraceptives).
  • Activating nociceptors on the free nerve endings of C fibers produces ischemic Pain


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 122, 142–147.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old girl with Type I diabetes develops a neuropathy limited to sensory neurons with free nerve endings. Quantitative sensory testing will reveal higher-than-normal thresholds for the detection of which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Temperature
  • Quantitative sensory testing will show higher-than-normal thresholds for the detection of Temperature.
  • Quantitative Sensory Testing (often called 'QST') allows us to measure changes in sensitivity to different types of sensations that can include temperature, touch, or pressure


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 141–143.

questions.stem: At which location along the basilar membrane are the highest-frequency sounds detected?

options.label: B
options.text: Farthest from the oval window, near the helicotrema

options.label: D
options.text: At the midpoint of the membrane

questions.solutionHtml:
Nearest the oval window

The feature of the traveling wave is that it travels fast along the initial portion of the basilar membrane but becomes progressively slower as it goes farther into the cochlea.





Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 675-76.

questions.stem: The brown-sequard syndrome is characterized by:

options.label: A
options.text: Fine touch lost on the opposite side

options.label: B
options.text: Pain and temperature loss on the same side

options.label: C
options.text: Pain and temperature loss on the opposite side

options.label: D
options.text: Only pain lost on the same side

questions.answerText: Pain and temperature loss on the opposite side
questions.solutionHtml:
Pain and temperature loss on the opposite side

 A functional hemisection of the spinal cord causes a characteristic and easily recognized clinical picture that reflects damage to ascending sensory (dorsal column pathway, ventrolateral spinothalamic tract) and descending motor (corticospinal tract) pathways, which is called the Brown-Séquard syndrome.

 




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page Number: 629

questions.stem: Due to a central cord lesion, the dissociated sensory loss is seen due to:

options.label: A
options.text: Decussating branches of lateral spinothalamic tract

questions.answerText: Decussating branches of lateral spinothalamic tract
questions.solutionHtml:
Decussating branches of lateral spinothalamic tract

Patients with this condition demonstrate a wide variety of neurological symptoms depending on where exactly the syrinx is located, but classically patients present with:

  • A cape-like loss of pain and temperature sensation along the back and arms, known as a ‘suspended sensory level’ disproportionately greater bilateral motor impairment in the upper compared to lower extremities.
  • This motor and sensory impairment can eventually cause atrophy, which begins in the hands and progresses proximally, resulting in deformities such as 'claw hands' and Charcot’s arthropathy


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 177

questions.stem: The distance by which two touch stimuli must be separated to be perceived as two separate stimuli is the greatest at?
questions.solutionHtml:
The lips

The distance by which two touch stimuli must be separated to be perceived as two separate stimuli is greatest at the lips rather than the fingertips. Areas with maximum Two Point Discrimination ability are - Lips, Fingers



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 153.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding triple response?

options.label: B
options.text: Flare is due to arteriolar dilation

questions.solutionHtml:
Both

The triple response consists of three aspects: Red spot, caused by capillary vasodilation. Flare is a redness in the surrounding area due to arteriolar dilation mediated by axon reflex. Wheal is caused by the exudation of extracellular fluid from capillaries and venules.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 581

options.label: D
options.text: Ipsilateral loss of crude touch sensation

questions.solutionHtml:
Ipsilateral loss of proprioception
